title: Source tax tariff: denomination, spouse employment and tariff code
purpose: Ask employees subject to source tax for their denomination, whether the spouse is gainfully employed and whether they have children. Combine these with the cross-border and child results into one tariff code (e.g. 'C1Y'), 'no tariff code', the Liechtenstein note, or 'incomplete - HR must complete'.

stories.title: Ask the religious denomination only where source tax needs it and derive the church-tax suffix
stories.i_want: the denomination of every employee who needs a source tax tariff code, and only of them, turned into the church-tax suffix Y or N
stories.so_that: the last letter of the tariff code is right, and nobody who is not subject to source tax is asked about their religion
stories.priority_reason: Without the denomination no tariff code can be computed, so HR would have to go back to the manual calculator step (D-001). Asking it of everyone would collect sensitive personal data that no party needs (G-01, F-hr_transcript-b84498).

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination is asked only of employees subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered the questions in steps 1 to 5 (about you, home address, nationality and C permit, civil status and spouse, cross-border commuting)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches step 6 'Source tax details'
acceptance_criteria.then: the denomination is asked, and required, only if the employee is subject to source tax. For employees who live in Liechtenstein it is asked only if they do not return daily and expect more than 45 work-related non-return days. Employees who are not subject to source tax, and Liechtenstein residents who in principle have no source tax liability, are not asked. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-040): for Liechtenstein residents the daily-return and 45-day questions come before the denomination, and the denomination is skipped when the answers mean 'in principle no source tax liability'.

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination offers exactly the calculator's two choices
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee chooses exactly one of 'Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed' or 'None or other'. The question cannot be left empty and no other denomination is collected.

acceptance_criteria.title: Church-tax suffix follows the denomination
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax has answered the denomination
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the church-tax suffix of the tariff code
acceptance_criteria.then: 'Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed' gives the suffix Y, and 'None or other' gives the suffix N. This follows the calculator's results (for example A0Y and A0N). The suffix is derived again whenever the denomination changes.

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination is used only for the source tax tariff
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered the denomination
acceptance_criteria.then: the denomination is recorded for HR only as the input to the source tax tariff code. It is not part of the pension fund registration. If a later answer means the employee is no longer asked the denomination, the answer is discarded on submission.

stories.title: Ask married employees and registered partners subject to source tax whether their spouse or partner works
stories.i_want: to know, for married employees and registered partners who need a tariff code, whether the spouse or partner is gainfully employed or receives replacement income
stories.so_that: the tariff letter is C (spouse employed) or B (spouse not employed), as in the calculator
stories.priority_reason: This answer decides the tariff letter for every married employee subject to source tax. Without it the tariff code cannot be computed and HR's manual calculator step comes back (D-001, F-hr_transcript-6a0a40).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse employment is asked only of married employees and registered partners who need a tariff code
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered civil status (step 4) and, if they live in Liechtenstein, the cross-border questions (step 5)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches step 6 'Source tax details'
acceptance_criteria.then: 'Is your spouse or registered partner gainfully employed or receiving replacement income?' is asked, and required, only if the employee is subject to source tax, is Married or in a Registered partnership, and (for Liechtenstein residents) has more than 45 non-return days. It is not asked of Single, Divorced, Widowed or Separated employees, of employees not subject to source tax, or of Liechtenstein residents who in principle have no source tax liability. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-003): for source tax a registered partnership counts as married and Separated counts as single, as in the calculator.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse employment is answered yes or no
acceptance_criteria.given: the spouse employment question is asked
acceptance_criteria.then: the answer is 'yes' or 'no' and cannot be left empty. 'yes' covers a spouse or partner who is gainfully employed or receives replacement income, as in the calculator's wording. The answer is recorded for HR only as the input to the source tax tariff letter (C for yes, B for no).

stories.title: Ask employees subject to source tax whether they have children
stories.i_want: to know whether an employee who needs a tariff code has biological or adopted children (for married employees and registered partners: the employee's or the spouse's/partner's)
stories.so_that: the child questions are asked only when there are children, and the child digit and the H tariff can be determined
stories.priority_reason: The child digit is part of every tariff code (D-001). Asking about children only of employees subject to source tax keeps to data minimisation (G-01, F-hr_transcript-b84498).

acceptance_criteria.title: The children question is asked only when the source tax details apply
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered steps 1 to 5
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches step 6 'Source tax details'
acceptance_criteria.then: the children question is asked, and required, only if the employee is subject to source tax and (for Liechtenstein residents) has more than 45 non-return days. It is asked of married and unmarried employees alike. It comes after the denomination and, for married employees and registered partners, after the spouse employment question, as in the calculator.

acceptance_criteria.title: Wording depends on civil status, answer is yes or no
acceptance_criteria.then: a Married employee or registered partner is asked whether they or their spouse/partner have biological or adopted children; a Single, Divorced, Widowed or Separated employee is asked whether they have biological or adopted children. The answer is 'yes' or 'no' and cannot be left empty. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-003): Registered partnership is asked like Married and Separated like Single, as in the calculator's two civil status groups.

acceptance_criteria.title: 'yes' opens the children step, 'no' gives child digit 0
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered the children question
acceptance_criteria.then: with 'yes' the employee goes on to step 7 'Children' (one block per child, no maximum number; a child's age is judged on the first working day, an assumption to be verified by a domain expert, D-044). With 'no' step 7 is skipped and no child counts towards the tariff code. The answer is recorded for HR only as an input to the source tax tariff code.

stories.title: Derive the base source tax tariff letter
stories.i_want: Lonio to derive the base tariff letter (A, B, C or H) from civil status, spouse employment and the children's results, following the calculator
stories.so_that: I no longer have to click through the Zurich calculator to find the tariff
stories.priority_reason: This replaces HR's manual calculator step, which is the product decision behind the tariff code (D-001, F-hr_transcript-34494f).

acceptance_criteria.title: Married employees and registered partners get C or B
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax is Married or in a Registered partnership
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the base tariff letter
acceptance_criteria.then: the letter is C if the spouse or partner is gainfully employed or receives replacement income, and B if not. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-003): a registered partnership counts as married, as in the calculator.

acceptance_criteria.title: Single, divorced, widowed and separated employees get H or A
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax is Single, Divorced, Widowed or Separated
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the base tariff letter
acceptance_criteria.then: the letter is H if at least one child counts with H (from the per-child results of step 7), and A otherwise, including when the employee has no children. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-003): Separated counts as single, as in the calculator. The per-child results follow observed calculator rows first (assumption D-046), and rows that were not observed are checked before go-live (see OQ-calculator-coverage).

acceptance_criteria.title: No replacement-income tariff
acceptance_criteria.given: any employee subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the base tariff letter
acceptance_criteria.then: the letter is never G, because a new employee always has earned income and replacement income is out of scope (D-006). Residence in Switzerland or in another country without cross-border rules gives the base letter directly, as in the calculator.

stories.title: Replace the base letter with the cross-border letter where the cross-border tariff applies
stories.i_want: employees living in Germany who meet the calculator's cross-border conditions to get the cross-border letter instead of the base letter
stories.so_that: cross-border commuters are taxed with the correct tariff
stories.priority_reason: Employees living in Germany are subject to source tax (F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a). A wrong letter gives a wrong tariff code, and Lonio now owns that result (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Without the cross-border tariff the base letter applies
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax for whom the cross-border tariff does not apply (anyone not living in Germany, and Germany residents who do not meet the cross-border conditions of step 5)
acceptance_criteria.then: the tariff letter is the base letter (A, B, C or H). For Germany residents the cross-border tariff does not apply when: they return daily without a certificate of residence ('not yet' counts as no, D-035); they do not return daily and a daily return is not reasonable; or a daily return is reasonable and they expect more than 60 non-return days. Liechtenstein residents never get a cross-border letter.

stories.title: Compute and record the full source tax tariff code
stories.i_want: Lonio to compute one complete Zurich tariff code (letter, child digit and church-tax suffix, e.g. 'C1Y') for every employee subject to source tax, and a clear text result for everyone else
stories.so_that: I no longer click through the calculator for each new employee and I can see at once who needs a tariff and which one
stories.priority_reason: This removes HR's manual calculator step for every employee (D-001, F-hr_transcript-34494f). Today HR does not know up front who has to answer the source tax questions (F-hr_transcript-b84498).

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees subject to source tax get a full tariff code
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is subject to source tax and is not a Liechtenstein resident who in principle has no source tax liability
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio computes the tariff code from the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.then: the result is one text made of the tariff letter (including the cross-border letter where it applies), the child digit (the number of children who count) and the church-tax suffix, for example 'C1Y', 'L0Y' or 'N1Y'. It is recorded for HR. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-051): the code is this single text. Like the calculator's result, the code is not legally binding.

acceptance_criteria.title: Liechtenstein residents: in principle no liability, or code subject to the double taxation agreement
acceptance_criteria.then: if the employee returns daily, or does not return daily and expects at most 45 non-return days, the result is the text 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR, and the step 6 questions are skipped. If the employee expects more than 45 non-return days, the result is the normal tariff code (never a cross-border letter), recorded with the note 'subject to the double taxation agreement' and flagged for HR. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-040, D-007). How HR handles the flag belongs to the later HR-side spec (D-034).

acceptance_criteria.title: Tariff code is always derived again from the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire and HR later changes an answer (for example a marriage, a new child, a move, or a certificate of residence handed in later)
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the tariff code again
acceptance_criteria.then: the tariff code reflects the latest answers. If the change means that questions apply that were never answered (for example the spouse employment question after a change to Married), the result is 'incomplete - HR must complete' instead of a code until HR enters the missing answers. Answers that no longer apply are discarded, as on the employee's submission. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-048). How HR makes these changes belongs to the later HR-side spec (D-034, D-037).

acceptance_criteria.title: Unexplored calculator paths are checked before go-live
acceptance_criteria.given: Lonio computes tariff codes on paths that were not observed in the calculator (the residence block for A/B/H, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N, and per-child results marked as inferred)
acceptance_criteria.when: the feature is prepared for go-live
acceptance_criteria.then: a domain expert compares Lonio's computed codes with the Zurich calculator for these paths before release (see OQ-calculator-coverage; a go-live condition that does not block this spec). Special tariffs such as D (second job) are out of scope for onboarding.
